title: Why Netflix Mailed DVDs for 10 Years
description: The slow advantage, explained with Netflix's DVD-to-streaming story.
facts_to_verify: Netflix started DVD-by-mail in 1998 and launched streaming in 2007
Netflix Prize: $1M recommendation contest announced in 2006
Streaming in 190+ countries after the January 2016 expansion

scenes.narration: Why did Netflix keep mailing DVDs for almost ten years?
Because the best companies build a slow advantage first, and only then make the big leap.
Every DVD they shipped taught them what people rent, what they finish, and what they skip. That data quietly became their real product.
In two thousand six, they even offered a million dollars to anyone who could improve their recommendations.
So when streaming launched in two thousand seven, they already had seven million subscribers and the data to keep them.
Then the leap. By twenty sixteen, Netflix was streaming in more than one hundred and ninety countries.
Subscribers grew from about seven million to over two hundred and thirty million.
The leap looked sudden. The advantage took ten years. So, why did Netflix keep mailing DVDs?

visual.text: The leap looked sudden. The advantage took ten years.
